Lesson 14.20 · 10 min · Verified 17 Jul 2026

Co-lending programme

After this lesson you can:
  • Operate the arrangement mechanics at journey level
  • Own allocation, escrow and reconciliation duties
On this page
  1. The product
  2. What a BA watches
  3. Journey contract
  4. Platform support
  5. Where this lives in LoanOS

1. The product

Module 8 taught the rules; this is the journey that runs them. The contract facts are the arrangement itself: originator and partner-lender references, shares in basis points (summing to 100% with the retention floor respected), the escrow account, the settlement waterfall, programme limits and per-loan allocation references.

Every lifecycle event — disbursement, EMI, charge, recovery — splits by share into partner subledgers, funded and settled through escrow per the waterfall.

2. What a BA watches

Reconciliation is the operating burden: partner statements, escrow movements and subledger legs must agree, with break management for when they don't. First-loss support arrangements (where present) interact with DLG rules — caps and classification duties from module 8 apply without dilution.

Regulatory anchors

  • RBI-CLA-2025 — Shares, retention floor, blended rate and escrow — enforced at journey level.
  • RBI-FUND-FLOW — Escrow is the permitted joint-funding channel.

Family IDs resolve in the India regulatory register (docs/compliance/india-regulatory-register.md), which owns sources and caveats.

Knowledge check

1. An EMI arrives on an 80/20 co-lent loan. What happens in accounting?

  1. It books to the originator
  2. It splits 80/20 into each partner's principal/interest/fee subledger legs and settles via the escrow waterfall
  3. It waits for month-end
  4. The bank keeps interest, the NBFC principal
Show answer

B. Loan-level allocation by share, per component, per event — reconciled through escrow — is the journey's operating core.
